tier_reason: The gonwan/webframework-benchmark readme table has libevhtp 1.2.18 / libevent 2.1.12 at 254k/s and Boost.Beast 1.83 at 220k/s. The code is public (libevhtp/libevhtp_server.c, beast/beast_server.cpp, their Dockerfiles, docker-compose.yml), the flags are gcc/g++ -O2 and the CPU is an AMD 7840HS. It is not A: no compiler version is stated (only the ubuntu:24.04 build-essential base image), and it is not B: it is a 0-star homemade suite, not a well-known one.

corrections.claimed_speedup: libevhtp 1.2.18 (on libevent 2.1.12): 254k req/s vs Boost.Beast 1.83: 220k req/s, about 1.15x higher throughput (derived from page data). Both are below nginx (336k/s) and Drogon (320k/s) in the same table.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: gcc -O2 (libevhtp server) and g++ -O2 (beast server), built in ubuntu:24.04 with build-essential per libevhtp/Dockerfile and beast/Dockerfile; compiler version not stated; no LTO. libevhtp 1.2.18 and libevent 2.1.12 are Ubuntu's prebuilt apt packages (libevhtp-dev, libevent-dev), so the library build flags are Ubuntu's.
corrections.caveats: Single-author homemade third-party benchmark (0-star repo gonwan/webframework-benchmark, Feb-Mar 2026), not independently reviewed; one wrk result per server, with no repeats or variance. Compiler version is not stated (ubuntu:24.04 build-essential, -O2), and libevhtp/libevent are distro-built binaries. The beast server is the Boost 1.83 http_server_async example: 4 threads share one io_context with per-connection strands, while libevhtp runs 4 worker threads plus a listener thread; the author says beast scaled poorly in an earlier run. The page says '12C host machine, AMD 7840HS', but the 7840HS is an 8-core/16-thread part, so the host core count is unclear. The gain is small (about 1.15x). libevhtp is archived, and its last commit is 2019-08-02.

notes: The numbers and the Beast comparison check out. The only substantive fix: flags are stated in the Dockerfiles (-O2), not missing as the record said. The license (BSD-3-Clause), 456 stars, archived status, last commit 2019-08-02 and the 1.2.18 tag all match gh. The readme numbers have been stable since commit 21f8cbf (2026-03-07).
